healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system funded through mandatory health insurance. Tourists pay out-of-pocket at affordable rates. Private clinics in Skopje offer good quality care. Public system is functional but underfunded.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Skopje provide good modern care. Public hospitals are adequate but may have long waits. Healthcare quality is reasonable in urban areas but limited in rural regions. Some doctors speak English, especially in private facilities.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies (аптека / apteka) generally open 8am-8pm weekdays, shorter hours on weekends. Some 24-hour pharmacies in Skopje.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are common in Skopje and Ohrid. Look for the green cross sign. Pharmacists may speak some English. Prices are affordable by Western standards. Many common medications available.
prescriptionRules: Prescription requirements are generally enforced. Antibiotics require a prescription. Basic pain relievers, cold medicines, and some stomach medications are available OTC.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substance. Carry a doctor's letter and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Require prescription. Documentation from your doctor recommended.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English for controlled medications. Original packaging is important. North Macedonia follows European pharmaceutical standards broadly.

travelInsurance.tips: Recommended for private hospital access and to avoid unexpected costs. Healthcare is affordable but insurance provides peace of mind, especially for adventure activities around Ohrid and Mavrovo.

recommended: Tick-borne encephalitis (for rural areas in spring-summer)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Routine vaccinations should be up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water in Skopje is generally safe to drink. Water quality in other areas varies — Ohrid tap water is usually fine. In rural areas, bottled water is recommended. Bottled water is cheap and widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Macedonian food is generally safe and delicious. Grilled meats (kebapi), tavche gravche (baked beans), and fresh salads are staples. Restaurant hygiene is generally good. Fresh produce at markets is safe when washed.
medicalTourismNote: North Macedonia is an emerging destination for dental tourism and cosmetic procedures, with prices significantly lower than Western Europe.
metaDescription: Health guide for North Macedonia: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: City General Hospital 8th September (Gradska Opshta Bolnica)
hospitals.notes: Largest public hospital in Skopje. Emergency department 24/7. Some English-speaking doctors.

hospitals.name: Sistina Hospital (Acibadem Sistina)
hospitals.notes: Leading private hospital. Modern equipment. English-speaking staff. International standards.

hospitals.name: Remedika Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital with good reputation. Multiple specialties. English spoken.

hospitals.name: Ohrid General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Public hospital serving the Ohrid region. Basic facilities adequate for emergencies. Macedonian spoken.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care in Skopje at very affordable prices. Dental tourism is growing.
dentalCare.costRange: $15-40 for consultation; $25-80 for fillings; $20-60 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Skopje offer good quality at a fraction of Western prices. Some cater specifically to foreign patients.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private dental clinics in Skopje accept walk-ins for emergencies. In Ohrid, the general hospital has a dental department.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited. Some private practitioners in Skopje speak English.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are developing. English-speaking therapists are scarce. Online therapy platforms may be the most practical option.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is improving but still limited. Skopje's newer areas have some ramps and accessible features. The Old Bazaar and historic areas have cobblestones and uneven surfaces.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Private hospitals like Sistina are accessible. Public hospitals have mixed accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public transport has limited accessibility. Taxis are the most practical option. Skopje is relatively flat in the center.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Ohrid's Old Town has steep cobblestone streets. The lakeside promenade is more accessible. Contact accommodations in advance about specific needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at clinics in Skopje.
covidStatus.notes: North Macedonia has lifted all COVID-related entry restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals provide detailed receipts and medical reports in English on request. Public hospitals may require additional effort to get documentation. Keep all receipts for insurance claims.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be lower. Actual costs vary by facility and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.note: Skopje hospitals handle most cases. Thessaloniki is only 2.5 hours by road and has excellent hospitals. Air evacuation available for critical cases.

pharmacyChains.name: Zegin Pharmacy
pharmacyChains.where: Multiple locations in Skopje and across North Macedonia
